title: Add sandbox policy reports to Copilot agent sessions
body:
## Summary

Add `/sandbox-policy` to Copilot agent-host sessions. The VS Code command invokes the SDK's existing `/sandbox policy` command and presents its effective policy as a persisted Markdown report, without starting a model turn or changing sandbox enforcement.

## User experience

- Offer `/sandbox-policy` in slash-command completion while keeping native `/sandbox` subcommands hidden.
- Show an **Open Sandbox Policy** link in the response that opens the formatted report in Markdown preview.
- Use normal theme-aware chat link colors, including hover and active states.
- Support mouse, Enter, and Space activation, with accessible-help guidance.
- Save a unique report for each invocation so earlier links continue to show their original snapshots.

## Implementation

- Introduce optional host-side `getInvocation` and `getOutput` hooks on resolved slash commands, separate from SDK catalog metadata. Omitted hooks or hooks returning `undefined` preserve the existing SDK invocation and output behavior.
- Support structured text and link output with optional Markdown and preview flags. Keep command lifecycle, mode handling, and runtime-settings invalidation in the session.
- Keep sandbox-specific argument validation, SDK mapping, policy formatting, and report persistence in `CopilotSandboxPolicyDisplay`.
- Strip ANSI styling, preserve SDK Markdown, format recognized terminal policy reports, and safely fence unrecognized plain text. Propagate invocation and file-write failures instead of emitting broken links.
- Preserve preview metadata across local and remote Agent Host URI rewriting without passing it to filesystem providers.
- Extract a reusable single-anchor rendering helper to avoid a second anchor scan. Repeated decoration does not register duplicate widgets or listeners.
- Reuse the shared SDK command type in completion handling.

## Compatibility

- Existing commands retain their default invocation and rendering when no custom behavior applies.
- Preserve native sandbox aliases and raw SDK input; do not format unrelated sandbox subcommands or client commands as policy reports.
- Reserve the host alias against runtime name collisions and keep it discoverable when SDK command discovery fails.
- No SDK dependency changes, new permissions, or sandbox-policy enforcement changes.

## Validation

- **803 targeted tests passed** across Copilot session, command-handler, completion, Markdown rendering, inline-anchor, URI adapter, and accessibility-help suites.
- Regression coverage includes local/remote preview links, rich links enabled/disabled, keyboard activation, report formatting and persistence, error propagation, optional-hook fallbacks, and duplicate-widget prevention.
- A 1,001-link regression test verifies a single anchor scan with 1,000 ordinary links and one preview link.
- Core typecheck and transpile watchers completed with zero errors.
- ESLint passed for changed refactor files; CSS lint passed with only pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Dark and light Component Explorer fixtures render without errors; preview-link colors were checked against regular chat links.
- `git diff --check` passed.

title: agentHost: isolate CopilotAgent tests from ambient COPILOT_HOME
body:
Fixes #335887

## Problem

Three `CopilotAgent` tests fail on a clean checkout when `COPILOT_HOME` is set:

| Test | Line |
| --- | --- |
| `resolves state files from the default and peer chat SDK backings` | 1323 |
| `a marker written after an initial read miss is picked up without a restart` | 8549 |

Clear `COPILOT_HOME` in a suite-level `setup` and restore it in `teardown`, so every test under `suite('CopilotAgent')` sees the injected home. title: mcp: stabilize discovery and coalesce migration refreshes
body:
## Summary

- Stop migration-panel refresh loops when multiple workspace roots define the same MCP server names.
- Collapse duplicate MCP notifications and migration refresh bursts instead of repeating discovery for every event.
- Cancel obsolete migration discovery when a newer refresh supersedes it or the editor closes, while preserving genuine updates and error reporting.

Fixes #335820

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Installed MCP discovery selected duplicate-name winners from the runtime-dependent display order. Publishing a winner moved it ahead of the other root's entry, which made the other entry win the next discovery pass. Replacing the runtime servers repeated this cycle.

Overlapping workbench subscriptions amplified each replacement into multiple notifications. The migration editor also observed several related inputs and started a computation for each notification. Its sequence guard discarded stale results only after the work had already happened.

### Implementation

- Discovery sorts a copy of the installed inventory by name and ID before applying existing scope precedence. Display ordering remains independent of discovery selection.
- One workbench observer handles runtime inventory and per-server enablement changes, re-sorts the display inventory, and emits the change notification.
- A zero-delay delayer coalesces migration refresh requests within a burst. The generation advances when a refresh is requested, immediately invalidating older work rather than waiting for the replacement computation to start.
- Each active refresh owns a cancellation token. It reaches file and MCP migration computation, destination-folder discovery, and MCP source-file reads. Cancelled planning stops before reading additional roots.
- Closing, recreating, or disposing the editor cancels pending work; reopening requests fresh migration information. Generation, session, harness, and cancellation checks prevent late results from being applied, including results from providers that do not cooperate with cancellation.

### Behavior and constraints

- Real configuration, enablement, and policy changes still trigger refreshes. This does not disable discovery or cache migration results indefinitely.
- Expected cancellation is not reported as a failure. Genuine computation errors remain visible and retryable.
- Scope precedence, display ordering, policy filters, workspace-root discovery exclusions, and guarded migration writes remain unchanged.
- The cross-root duplicate-name migration restriction tracked by #335884 is intentionally unchanged; this change fixes refresh behavior, not which same-name entries may migrate.

</details>

title: Validate OSC 633 CWD reports with shell integration nonces
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335858

- Require process-terminal OSC 633 CWD updates to carry the terminal's exact, non-empty shell integration nonce; ignore missing, empty, or mismatched reports while preserving the prior CWD.
- Keep nonce-less CWD reports working for extension-owned and custom pseudoterminals, while marking those updates as untrusted.
- Keep nonce-less reports from manually integrated nested or relayed process shells rejected because the nonce is intentionally removed from the environment; those shells may retain the parent CWD until a trusted report resumes.
- Update the compatibility policy when a terminal is reused, so process and custom-PTY tasks cannot inherit each other's behavior.
- Carry extension ownership through remote launch transport and persistent process details.
- Apply the same compatibility policy in the PTY-host recorder so completed and partial command CWD metadata survives replay.
- Restore extension ownership through an ownership-only process property before persistent replay, without overwriting the restored executable, arguments, environment, or CWD.
- Append the same nonce to serialized CWD reports from Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell, and task startup.
- Keep the Fish nonce in global shell scope so prompt hooks can include it after initialization.
- Emit the PowerShell CWD nonce as prompt output, matching the existing nonce-bearing `EnvJson` report; Windows 10 prompt rendering still requires manual verification.
- Rewrite task `initialText` to the live or persisted terminal nonce during reuse and reconnection for both string and object forms.
- Keep Agent Host property parsing compatible with the optional nonce without including it in the decoded CWD or changing terminal-management policy.
- Keep OSC 7, OSC 9;9, OSC 1337, and Agent Host CWD trust policy unchanged; this PR is scoped to Workbench OSC 633 handling.

## Testing

- Passed 57 targeted Node tests with 9 expected platform skips, covering PTY-host recorder metadata, reattach/revive ordering, remote server transport, Agent Host parser compatibility, and shell emitters.
- Passed 188 targeted Electron tests with 2 existing pending cases, covering strict process-terminal validation, live reuse transitions, remote client transport, persistent extension-terminal reconstruction, old editor-state hydration, serialized delimiters, task startup, and reused-terminal nonce rewriting.
- Passed Bash, Zsh, and Fish syntax and runtime checks.
- Passed `transpile-client`, targeted ESLint, full repository hygiene, and diff checks.
- PowerShell runtime was unavailable on macOS. Its source emission is covered by the terminal environment test suite, but visible prompt rendering on Windows 10 has not been manually verified.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- OSC 633 CWD argument framing comes from [`ShellIntegrationAddon` property handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L571-L590); this keeps the serialized property in the first argument and the terminal nonce in the second.
- Separate nonce framing follows the existing shell command reports in [Bash](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-bash.sh#L350-L356), [Zsh](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration-rc.zsh#L256-L260), [Fish](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.fish#L104-L119), and [PowerShell](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1#L134-L145).
- Task CWD serialization and nonce placement follow [`taskShellIntegrationStartSequence`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L182-L201).
- Reconnection handling builds on the existing task-terminal reuse flow in [`terminalTaskSystem.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/tasks/browser/terminalTaskSystem.ts#L1592-L1603).
- PTY-host command metadata persistence follows the existing [`XtermSerializer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L1033-L1059) and process-detail reconstruction path in [`PtyService`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L638-L664).
- Remote ownership transport follows the existing client mapping in [`RemoteTerminalBackend`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/remoteTerminalBackend.ts#L184-L197) and server mapping in [`RemoteTerminalChannel`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/server/node/remoteTerminalChannel.ts#L193-L211).
- Ownership-only editor hydration follows the existing process-property dispatch in [`TerminalInstance`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts#L1558-L1583).
- Agent Host compatibility parsing follows the existing command-line nonce separation in [`Osc633Parser`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ce1e1cefcf8708bd01d9cf8fa9fc6b5a6d22c260/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/osc633Parser.ts#L122-L138).

title: [cherry-pick] Tighten artifact registration guidance
body:
Cherry-pick of #335631 from `main`.

Updates the `add_artifact_or_reference` tool description, `isArtifact` input description, and first-turn `ARTIFACT_TOOLS_INSTRUCTION` so the model has a clear eligibility test for what to register.

**Problem:** the current text says artifacts are "notable results you produced beyond ordinary workspace edits, such as a report written outside the workspace." That makes location the signal, so anything persisted outside the workspace (scratch JSON, run-tracking records, cached data) reads as registrable.

**Change:**
- Register only deliverables the user requested, or standalone results they are clearly likely to reopen, download, or reuse.
- Default to no registration; it's not an inventory of everything saved.
- Explicitly exclude scratch files, caches, logs, intermediate results, and configuration snapshots unless requested.
- State that persistence or location outside the workspace is not an eligibility signal.
- Never create, copy, or relocate a file solely to have something to register.

Prose-only change; all phrases pinned by existing tests are preserved. `artifactServerTools.test.ts` and `chatContributions.test.ts` pass.

title: fix: centre the fork tooltip on the fork button
body: Fixes #335740 | Before | After | |---|---| | | | #335072 centred the fork glyph; this centres the tooltip. Three independent causes, each measured on a real hover in a running build. **1. The separator inflated the hover target — `chat.css`, −3.8px** The `·` was an in-flow `::before` on `.chat-fork-action-item`, so the managed hover anchored to a box spanning `dot + 4px gap + button`. It now draws in the item's left gutter (`position: absolute; right: 100%`, gutter reserved with `margin-left`), leaving the item's border box equal to the button — hover target width 36.71px → 29.14px, net layout shift **+0.44px**. `pointer-events: none` also makes the dot inert; it was previously a click target for Fork. **2. Caret rounding on odd tooltip widths — `hoverWidget.ts`, +0.5px** The hover is positioned unrounded (`target.center.x - clientWidth / 2`) but the caret was placed at `Math.round(hoverWidth / 2)`. Since `_x` is itself fractional, that rounding could never snap the caret to a device pixel — it only broke the centring. Removed on both axes. **3. Caret half-width vs `PointerSize` under zoom — `hover.css`, −0.25px** `PointerSize` (3) is treated as the caret's half-width, but its `1px` borders round down to whole device pixels under zoom, leaving a 5.86px box centred at 2.93px. Sizing it as a `border-box` 6px square keeps the centre at exactly `PointerSize` at any zoom. The `.locked` variant drops its `width/height: 4px` (which would now mean a 4px *border* box) and is visually unchanged. ### Verification Measured against each hover's real anchor element, every pointer tooltip now centres within **0.011px**, independent of width parity and zoom. Before: odd-width tooltips +0.5px, fork button −3.78px. Note: several controls anchor their hover to a parent rather than the visible `.action-label` (Toggle Chat uses `DIV.action-container`), so measuring the inner element reports a spurious ~0.5px. ### Tests `chatForkActionViewItem.test.ts` gains a case rendering the fork item as a **non-first** toolbar item so `:not(:first-child)` applies, asserting the item's box equals the button's box and the separator is out of flow and not hit-testable. Verified it fails on the pre-fix CSS. 193 passing across the fork and hover suites; `hygiene` and `stylelint` clean.

title: Improve Copilot BYOK reliability and reasoning support
body:
## Summary

Improve the reliability of bring-your-own-key (BYOK) chat providers in the Copilot extension. The changes cover credential migration, conversation preservation, reasoning capability discovery and request serialization, incremental tool-call delivery, and OpenAI-compatible response handling.

**This is a draft for scope and implementation review, not a merge-ready change.** There is no linked tracking issue yet. The branch contains several independently committed fixes and reasoning support changes; in accordance with the contribution guidelines, issue association and separation into focused PRs need to be resolved before requesting final review.

## Changes

### Credential migration and logging
- Wait for provider-group migration to succeed before deleting the legacy API key.
- Share an in-flight migration between callers, retain the source credential on failure, and allow a later retry.
- Handle migration failures initiated during provider construction without logging credentials.
- Omit invalid custom header values from warning messages.

### Conversation history and endpoint cloning
- Validate Responses state markers before trimming conversation history, including the zero-data-retention path.
- Match Gemini tool results to complete call IDs instead of deriving function names from ID prefixes; reject orphan results and conflicting function names.
- Preserve multiple nonempty Gemini system instructions in their original order.
- Clone nested token-limit metadata without mutating the original endpoint, preserving Azure authentication and OpenRouter routing.

### Reasoning capabilities and requests
- Centralize BYOK reasoning option resolution across supported providers, including default enabling, explicit disabling, and supported effort selection.
- Merge live model capabilities with known metadata, and expose applicable reasoning controls without treating missing metadata as an explicit capability value.
- Serialize provider-specific reasoning controls for Chat Completions, Responses, native Anthropic/Gemini, OpenRouter, and configurable OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Reject unsupported explicit-disable requests instead of silently ignoring them.
- Forward visible reasoning independently of whether encrypted reasoning metadata is requested.

### Tool streaming and endpoint compatibility
- Forward tool-call start events and incremental argument updates through the language-model wrapper and contributed endpoint, before the final tool call is available.

title: Fix keymap change events being dropped by debounce merge
body:
The merge function for the debounced extension-change event in extensionsUtils used `result.some(l => !areSameExtensions(l, identifier))`. That is false for an empty accumulator, so the first change in every debounce window was dropped and the event always fired `[]`. The disable-other-keymaps check downstream never ran.

This collects identifiers that are not already present instead, and extracts the merge so it is covered by a unit test.

title: Fix infinite loop in strings.count with empty substring
body:
count(value, '') never terminates: indexOf('') keeps returning the same index, and advancing by substr.length (0) makes no progress, so the loop spins forever.

This returns 0 early for an empty substring, matching the guards ltrim and rtrim already have. All existing callers pass non-empty literals, so behavior elsewhere is unchanged.

Also adds the first unit tests for count.

title: Fix language-specific overrides with falsy values being ignored
body:
Language-specific overrides could crash the override computation and silently drop explicit values: `createOverrideConfigurationModel` used a truthiness check on override values, and its `typeof x === 'object'` guards treat `null` as an object.

What this fixes:

- A `null` base value overridden with an object threw `TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator ... in null` out of `mergeContents`. Reproduced through the real settings parser (`ConfigurationModelParser.parse` on `{"a": null, "[x]": {"a": {"b": 1}}}`) — the new regression test throws before this change and passes after it.
- Explicit falsy overrides (`0`/`false`/`''`/`null`) at the model level fell back to the base value instead of winning. Covered by a model-level regression test.

One correction to the original description: dotted keys like `editor.tabSize` were already safe. Parsed settings go through `toValuesTree` (`toOverrides`), so the outer override value is a truthy parent object and `mergeContents` already preserves nested falsy values — I verified this path is unaffected. The fix hardens the model-level contract and removes the `null` crash.

The change itself: presence check is now `!== undefined`, and the merge guard uses the existing `types.isObject` helper (the same one `mergeContents` already uses).

title: Do not open inline math on an escaped dollar sign in markdown
body:
Fixes #335663

An escaped `\$` in a Markdown paragraph opened an inline math span, because the lookbehind `(?<=\s|\W|^)(?<!\$)` accepts a preceding backslash (`\` matches `\W`) and only rejects a preceding `$`. The span then swallowed everything up to the next bare `$`, so inline code spans after the first `\$` lost their highlighting.

This adds `(?<!\\)` to the lookbehind of `math_inline_single` and `math_inline_double`. The other rules are not affected: `math_inline_block` and both rules in `md-math-block.tmLanguage.json` require whitespace or line start directly before the `$`, and `md-math-fence.tmLanguage.json` does not match `$` at all.

Limitation: the check only looks at one character, so `\\$` (an escaped backslash followed by a real `$`) is now also rejected as an opener. The rest of this grammar and the base Markdown grammar do not count backslashes either, so this keeps the same approximation.

**Testing**

- New fixtures in `md-math.md`: `\$ ... \$` and `\$\$ ... \$\$` with a code span after them (not math, code span highlighted), and `$x+y$` (still math). Results file regenerated; the 600 existing entries are unchanged, 33 entries were appended.

title: Fix repeated silent authentication failures caused by stale refresh tokens
body:
Fixes #335639

## Problem

I investigated this after Settings Sync continued to show “Sign in to Sync Settings” following a successful Microsoft sign-in on macOS. Logs showed `createSession` returning a session, followed by `getSessions` returning no sessions after `AADSTS700082`. I can no longer reproduce the original sign-in failure with my real account. Instead, the tests use a simulated account, synthetic tokens, and simulated identity-server responses with the real MSAL library and VS Code authentication code to reproduce the token-cache defect described below. The same regression tests fail on the original code and pass with the proposed fix.

The Microsoft authentication extension's current MSAL dependency can repeatedly reload a rejected refresh token from persisted storage. MSAL removes the token from memory on an `invalid_grant` / `bad_token` response, but does not call the persistence callback on that failure path.

When a rejected family refresh token coexists with a fresh application refresh token for the same account, repeated silent requests keep submitting the family token and failing despite the fresh credential being available.

## Reproduction

See [#335639](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335639) for the reproduction steps, expected results before and after the fix, and an auxiliary standalone MSAL reproduction.

## Fix

Persist MSAL's removal of the rejected token before retrying silent authentication once, within the existing PCA sequencer. Apply this to ordinary silent acquisition and ID-token refresh. Broker authentication and unrelated errors keep their existing behavior.

If the persisted cache changed while the request was in flight, reload it instead of writing the failed request's snapshot. This check is not atomic with the subsequent write, so a concurrent update between them can still be overwritten. A concurrent cache change can also exhaust the retry, requiring a subsequent session request.

title: [Early POC] Add a third-party Canvas MVP for Copilot agent sessions
body:
## Summary

Add a desktop MVP for third-party Copilot Canvases using the existing Copilot runtime extension format and VS Code's Integrated Browser, with the normal browser navigation bar left visible.

### Architecture

The Node SDK runs in Agent Host and talks to the Copilot runtime. The runtime discovers compatible extensions, launches their backend processes, and owns their Canvas tools and lifecycle. An extension supplies an HTTP(S) URL, which VS Code renders in the Integrated Browser. This change adds the host/client plumbing and UI; it does not reimplement Canvas execution or modify the runtime.

- Project live SDK Canvas events and snapshots into typed per-chat session metadata, including reopen revisions and unavailable instances.
- Add ownership-validated catalog/open/close operations. Local clients use the management channel; remote clients use capability-gated extension RPCs.
- Reuse existing provisional-chat materialization and dormant-chat resume for direct opening, without synthesizing a prompt or starting a model turn.
- Present local Canvases in transient, ephemeral-storage browser tabs. Hiding a tab does not close the runtime instance; explicit Close Canvas does. Runtime URLs are not persisted as normal browser tabs.
- Add **editor + > Canvas > Open Canvas... / Reopen Canvas... / Close Canvas...**, plus corresponding Chat commands.
- Use a native picker for the runtime catalog, with explicit Refresh and JSON input when an extension declares an input schema. Runtime schema validation remains authoritative.
- Include AI-disabled and new-chat menu gating, accessibility help, tests, and architecture documentation.

### SDK prerequisite

Companion SDK change: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/pull/2618.

The current installed Node SDK (1.0.13) does not expose a usable extension-launch callback. The companion SDK draft adds `onExtensionLaunch` and startup registration of the existing runtime launch-provider protocol.

VS Code's `copilotExtensionLaunch.ts` only supplies an executable, the runtime's own bundled bootstrap, and the extension entrypoint. Discovery, permission enforcement, spawning, and termination remain runtime-owned.

Standalone extension loading is enabled only when the SDK advertises `supportsExtensionLaunchProvider`. **This draft does not update the package dependency and will not provide standalone Canvas extensions with the stock SDK.** It needs the companion SDK built locally for testing, then a dependency update after that change ships.

The local demo used `VSCODE_DEV_INJECT_NODE_MODULE_LOOKUP_PATH` with an ignored node-modules overlay pointing `@github/copilot-sdk` at the built sibling SDK checkout. No machine-specific dependency paths or overlay files are committed. Setup details are documented in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md`.

## Validation performed during implementation

- 320 focused backend tests passed.
- 86 focused UI/presentation/accessibility/terminal tests passed; 45 directly affected tests passed again after the final menu-gating update. These runs overlap and are not additive.
- Core typecheck/editor diagnostics, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Live OSS validation with the patched SDK: menu opening without a chat turn, actual rendered counter with the standard navigation bar, tab hide/reopen, supported window reload/reopen, and explicit runtime close with server shutdown.
- Fresh-chat model-driven validation: `list_canvas_capabilities`, `open_canvas`, and one approved `invoke_canvas_action` increment completed; the server and assistant both returned count **1**.

## Known limitations / follow-up

- **One restored demo conversation stalls after accepting messages.** This remains unresolved. A fresh conversation in the same profile successfully completed both normal chat and Canvas-tool requests; the restored conversation was preserved for investigation. This draft is not claiming all restore/turn lifecycle cases are ready to ship.
- An earlier raw automation `page.reload()` was followed by aborted browser-navigation notifications. A full app restart and supported **Developer: Reload Window** validation did not reproduce those errors; the raw-reload behavior has not been fixed.
- Desktop/local presentation only. Remote catalog/open/close plumbing exists, but remote Canvas presentation and loopback forwarding are intentionally unsupported.
- Opening from the menu requires an existing local Copilot chat; an uncreated new-chat composer is not implicitly turned into a runtime session.
- App-native Canvas types, installation/import/discovery management UI, and navigation-bar hiding are deferred.
- No privileged page bridge is introduced; Canvas pages remain untrusted browser content.

Kept as a draft to share the architecture and MVP for review before SDK/API stabilization and lifecycle hardening.

body:
Fixes #290708

Related to #299540 (same underlying root cause, reported independently).

## Bug

When multiple VS Code windows are open, one per Git worktree, operations that write into a linked worktree's private Git metadata — such as `git commit` with `core.editor` set to `code --wait`, or a rebase — can open the editor in the main worktree's window instead of the linked worktree's window.

## Root cause

`findWindowOnFile` normally selects a window by checking whether the target file is a child of an open window's folder. Git linked worktrees store their private per-worktree files under the main worktree's `.git/worktrees/<name>/` directory, so those files appear to belong to the main worktree rather than the linked worktree.

## Fix

Recognize Git linked-worktree metadata paths before the existing parent-folder matching and resolve the linked worktree through its `.git` pointer file. The comparison uses the full resolved worktree metadata path so unrelated repositories with the same worktree name cannot be confused.

Ordinary repositories, normal files, non-file URIs, and existing fallback behavior remain unchanged.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:
- linked-worktree metadata routing to the correct window
- fallback to existing behavior when there is no matching linked-worktree window
- paths that merely resemble Git worktree metadata
- two unrelated repositories using the same worktree name

## Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed
- Node syntax checks on both changed files — passed
- Standalone algorithm verification — 6/6 assertions passed

No compatible Node version manager or vendored Node binary was available, so no dependency installation was attempted. CI/maintainer validation is therefore requested for the full test suite.
